info.title: REALAX API
info.description: Transaction automation for Ontario realtors. Generated from the Zod schemas in src/schemas — do not hand-edit.

error.description: Stable machine-readable code. Branch on this, not on `message`.

address.example: 55 Yonge Street, Suite 400, Toronto, ON M5E 1J4

brokerage.description: The selected preset, or null when the agent has not picked one.

brokerageId.description: Id of a brokerage from GET /api/agent/brokerages, or null to detach.

propertyId.description: Set in build plan 1.4, when a property is attached. Null on a fresh draft.

mlsNumber.description: Null for a property entered by hand rather than found on the board.

property.description: Null on a draft that has not had a property attached yet.

partyCount.description: Parties still on the transaction. Removed ones are not counted.

search.description: Free text over the property address, city and MLS number. Case-insensitive, matches anywhere in the value.

status.description: Repeatable. Any of the given statuses matches.

type.description: Only LISTING is wired. Purchase and Lease are shown in the picker and marked as coming next; the API refuses them.

mlsNumber.description: The listing this was autofilled from, when it was autofilled at all.

id.description: Identifies this party on this transaction. Use it for the item routes under /api/transactions/{id}/parties.

personId.description: The underlying person record. Distinct from `id` because build plan 2.5 reuses one person across transactions; today there is exactly one party per person.

signingOrder.description: Position in the signing sequence (build plan 3.1 signs one signer at a time). Null until the order is set.

dateOfBirth.description: As printed on the identity document. Date only — no time, no timezone.

fullLegalName.description: The name as it appears on identification and as it will be filled on the form.

signingOrder.description: Position in the signing sequence. Left null until the order is decided.

purchasePriceWords.description: The same figure spelled out. The form prints both, and the words govern.
purchasePriceWords.example: One Million Two Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand

depositHolder.description: The brokerage holding the deposit in trust.

schedulesList.description: Which schedules form part of the agreement.

hstTreatment.description: Whether HST is included in or in addition to the purchase price.

coopBrokerageName.example: Bayview Heights Real Estate Ltd., Brokerage

sellerLawyerAddress.example: 120 Adelaide Street West, Suite 900, Toronto, ON M5H 1T1

buyerLawyerAddress.example: 75 Front Street East, Suite 300, Toronto, ON M5E 1B8

field.description: Stable identifier. For a form blank it is the name the curated template gives it; for a rule about the transaction itself it is the rule. Branch on this, not on `label`.

label.description: What an agent calls this field. Safe to show as-is.

areaLabel.description: The name of the page that fixes it, for the link text.

failures.description: Empty when the check passed. Ordered as the form prints, which is the order an agent works down it.

revision.description: The OREA revision the template is pinned to.

available.description: Whether a filled PDF exists to download.

filledCount.description: Fields that had a value at the last fill, out of `fieldCount`. Fields, not blanks on the page: the four ruled lines under CHATTELS INCLUDED are one field, and how many of them the text needs is the fill engine's business.

fieldCount.description: Fields this form asks the agent for. The same set the compliance gate reports against, so the two agree.

truncated.description: Blanks whose value would not fit and was cut down to it, even after shrinking. Empty on a normal fill, and worth showing when it is not: the document says less than the agent typed.

fileName.description: A sensible name to save it as. Carries no client detail.

IdentityDocumentType.description: Narrow on purpose: FINTRAC names particular documents, and a scan of something else is not a verification however well it reads.

documentNumberRead.description: Whether a document number was read. The number itself is never returned; it is encrypted at rest and stays server-side.

confidence.description: The lowest confidence across the fields that were found, 0–100. The lowest rather than the mean, because a result where everything is certain except the document number is exactly the result to check.

lowConfidence.description: Below the threshold at which the agent should read every field rather than skim.

partyId.description: The person this verifies, not the party-on-a-transaction row.

documentNumberOnFile.description: Whether a document number is held. The number is encrypted at rest and is never returned by this API, in any form.

verifiedMethod.description: The FINTRAC method used, and how the record was filled: `government_photo_id` when a reading assisted it, `government_photo_id_manual` when a person typed every value off the card. Both are the same method — the agent looked at a government photo ID either way — and the service decides which from what the reading produced, never the caller. `demo_override` is not a FINTRAC method at all: it is written only by the demo-mode button, which marks a party verified with no document and nobody examining anything, and a record carrying it must be shown as what it is rather than as a verification. Left as a string rather than an enum so that a value written by an older build cannot fail to parse on the way out.

expired.description: The document had expired as of this reading. A verification on an expired document is not one.

scanId.description: Identifies this reading while it awaits confirmation. Confirming it is what creates the record.

scanned.description: What the reader made of the image, or null when it could find no document in it. Null is not an error: the file is stored and the scan is confirmable, the agent simply types the document out instead of correcting a reading, and the record then says it was filled by hand.

allOf.description: As confirmed by the agent, which may not be what was uploaded or read.

expiryDate.description: As confirmed by the agent. Null when the document has no expiry or none could be read and the agent left it blank.

AttentionKind.description: `compliance_blocked` — the last compliance check on a form failed, and `count` is how many fields it named. `identity_missing` — `count` parties on the transaction have no identity record, which is FINTRAC exposure. `stale_draft` — a draft nobody has touched, and `count` is how many days.

count.description: What the kind says it counts. Never zero — a row with nothing behind it is not a row.

get.description: Unauthenticated. 200 while the service and all three dependencies (Postgres, Redis, S3) answer; 503 with the same body shape when any of them does not.

200.description: Service and every dependency are up

503.description: Service is up but at least one dependency is down

get.summary: The brokerage presets available on the profile form
get.description: Requires a session. Reference data, ordered by name — the profile form renders it as a select, and the selected entry supplies the address and phone displayed next to it.

post.description: Unauthenticated. On success sets an httpOnly session cookie; the response body carries no token. Agent accounts only — there are no roles and no brokerage admin.
Unauthenticated by design — calling it without a session is a no-op that still returns 200, so a client clearing stale state never has to handle a 401.

get.summary: The agent owning the current session
get.description: Requires a session. The frontend route guard calls this: a 401 is the signal to redirect to the login page.

401.description: No session, or the session refers to an agent that no longer exists

get.description: Requires a session. Always the caller's own profile — there is no agent id in the path, because there is no way to read anyone else's.

200.description: The profile, with the selected brokerage resolved

patch.description: Requires a session. Partial: an absent field is unchanged, an explicit null clears it. Returns the saved profile, so the client renders what was stored rather than what it sent.

400.description: Body failed validation, or brokerageId names a brokerage that does not exist

get.description: Requires a session. Scoped to the caller — there is no agent filter, because there is no way to read another agent's transactions. Newest first unless ordered otherwise. Every query parameter is optional; with none of them this is the whole list, one page at a time. Filtering happens here rather than in the browser so that a filtered list is a link that survives a reload, and so that an agent with years of deals is not sent all of them.

post.summary: Fill a form, if the compliance gate passes
post.description: Requires a session, and the transaction must belong to the caller. The compliance gate runs FIRST. If it fails the answer is 422 carrying the failure list and nothing is drawn — no PDF, not even a partial one. There is no override and no force flag. On a pass the form is drawn, stored, and the row moves to FILLED.

404.description: No such transaction, or no curated template for that form

422.description: The compliance gate blocked the fill. `compliance.failures` is the list to show the agent; nothing was written.

message.example: 7 things need attention before this form can be filled

get.summary: A form's status on a transaction
get.description: Requires a session, and the transaction must belong to the caller. A form that has never been filled answers 200 with status DRAFT and `available` false rather than 404 — the form exists for the transaction as soon as the template does.

404.description: No such transaction, or no curated template for that form

get.summary: A short-lived link to the filled form
get.description: Requires a session, and the transaction must belong to the caller. Issues a presigned URL valid for a few minutes. Nothing in the bucket is public; this is the only way a filled form is read.

404.description: No such transaction, or the form has not been filled

get.summary: What is stopping this form from being filled
get.description: Requires a session, and the transaction must belong to the caller. The same verdict the fill endpoint gates on, without filling anything and without recording a check — this is what a page reads to show each section as complete or not.

404.description: No such transaction, or no curated template for that form

post.summary: Mark a party verified without verifying anybody — demo builds only
post.description: Requires a session, and the transaction must belong to the caller. **This exists only so the transaction can be walked end to end while there is no working document reader.** It writes an `IdentityRecord` with no document, no number and nobody having examined anything, so that the identity tile stops blocking the deal. The route is mounted only when the API runs with `DEMO_MODE=true`, and the API refuses to start with that flag on when `NODE_ENV=production`; on every other build this path does not exist and answers 404. The record it writes carries `verifiedMethod: demo_override`, which is not a FINTRAC method — it never matches a query for real verifications, and any screen showing it must show it as a demo override rather than as a verification. A party that already has a record is a conflict, so this can never leave a fabricated record sitting beside a real one.

201.description: The demo-override record, which verifies nobody

404.description: No such transaction or party — or a build without demo mode, where this route does not exist

409.description: That party already has an identity record

post.summary: Upload and read a party’s identity document
post.description: Requires a session, and the transaction must belong to the caller. Multipart: `document` is the image and `documentType` says what it is. The file is stored in the Canadian bucket under SSE-KMS first and read from there, so the record is provably about the stored object. The document number is encrypted before it reaches a column and is never returned. **This does not verify anybody:** it answers with what was read and a `scanId`, and the `IdentityRecord` is created only when the agent confirms that reading. An image no document could be read from is not an error — it answers 201 with a null `scanned`, and the agent types the document out and confirms that.

document.description: JPEG or PNG, at most 5 MB.

201.description: What was read — or null when nothing could be — awaiting the agent’s confirmation

400.description: No file, an unsupported type, or a document type that is not accepted

404.description: No such transaction, or no such party on it

get.summary: The identity records held for a party
get.description: Requires a session, and the transaction must belong to the caller. Records are held against the person, so a party verified on an earlier transaction is already verified here — that reuse is the point of build plan 2.5. Document numbers are never included.

404.description: No such transaction, or no such party on it

post.summary: Read an identity document before the party exists
post.description: Requires a session, and the transaction must belong to the caller. The scan-first flow: an agent adding a party photographs the licence, and the reading fills the form that creates them — which has to happen in this order, because the name is the thing being read and it is also the one field a party cannot be created without. The scan is held with no party attached and becomes that person’s when it is confirmed through their party. Identical to the per-party scan in every other respect, including that it verifies nobody and that an image with no document in it answers 201 with a null `scanned`.

document.description: JPEG or PNG, at most 5 MB.

201.description: What was read — or null when nothing could be — awaiting a party and a confirmation

400.description: No file, an unsupported type, or a document type that is not accepted

404.description: No such transaction

post.summary: Confirm a reading, creating the identity record
post.description: Requires a session, and the transaction must belong to the caller. The agent has read the document and checked it against the card; this writes the `IdentityRecord` from what they confirmed. Nothing is verified until this call — an uploaded scan that is never confirmed stays a reading. Confirming twice is a conflict rather than a second record: the reading is one event. A scan taken before the party existed is attached to the party here; one already attached to a different party on the same transaction is not confirmable through this one, and answers 404.

201.description: The identity record the agent’s confirmation created

400.description: The confirmed values are not valid

404.description: No such transaction or party, or no such scan available to this party

409.description: That scan has already been confirmed

get.summary: Everything the agent's home page shows
get.description: Requires a session. Scoped to the caller. One request rather than six: the home page is the first screen of the product and fanning its blocks out from the browser would make it the slowest. Counts cover every status including the ones at zero, so the row of tiles does not change shape as the day goes on. The attention list is capped and ordered most-blocking first — it is a list to act on, not a report.

200.description: Counts, what needs attention, and the most recently touched transactions
